claim: During anaphase B spindle elongation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe, the sliding motor Klp9 (kinesin-6) promotes microtubule growth in vivo.
source: We show that during anaphase B spindle elongation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe, the sliding motor Klp9 (kinesin-6) also promotes microtubule growth in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experiments using monopolar spindles showing reduced microtubule bundle growth upon klp9 deletion.

claim: In vitro, Klp9 can enhance and dampen microtubule growth, depending on the tubulin concentration.
source: In vitro, Klp9 can enhance and dampen microtubule growth, depending on the tubulin concentration.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro reconstitution assays showing Klp9 increases growth at low tubulin concentration and decreases growth at high tubulin concentration.

claim: Klp9 is able to promote and block tubulin subunit incorporation into the microtubule lattice in order to set a well-defined microtubule growth velocity.
source: This indicates that the motor is able to promote and block tubulin subunit incorporation into the microtubule lattice in order to set a well-defined microtubule growth velocity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Klp9 can both increase and decrease microtubule growth velocity depending on conditions.

claim: Klp9 recruitment to spindle microtubules is dependent on its dephosphorylation mediated by XMAP215/Dis1.
source: Moreover, Klp9 recruitment to spindle microtubules is dependent on its dephosphorylation mediated by XMAP215/Dis1, a microtubule polymerase, creating a link between the regulation of spindle length and spindle elongation velocity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing reduced Klp9 recruitment upon dis1 deletion and rescue by phospho-deficient Klp9 mutant.

claim: Dis1 is a microtubule polymerase.
source: Moreover, Klp9 recruitment to spindle microtubules is dependent on its dephosphorylation mediated by XMAP215/Dis1, a microtubule polymerase, creating a link between the regulation of spindle length and spindle elongation velocity.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work showing Dis1 as a microtubule polymerase.

claim: Klp9 has a dual-function in regulating microtubule sliding and microtubule growth, allowing an inherent coordination of both processes.
source: Collectively, we unravel the mechanism of anaphase B, from Klp9 recruitment to the motors dual-function in regulating microtubule sliding and microtubule growth, allowing an inherent coordination of both processes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing Klp9 generates sliding forces and regulates microtubule growth velocity.

claim: During anaphase B, the spindle elongates to push apart the spindle poles and separate the two chromosome sets.
source: During anaphase B, the spindle elongates to push apart the spindle poles and separate the two chromosome sets (Mallavarapu et al., 1999; Oegema et al., 2001; Roostalu et al., 2010; Scholey et al., 2016; Straight et al., 1998; Vukušić et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In Ustilago maydis and Ptk1 cells, spindle elongation is mainly achieved through cortical pulling forces acting on astral microtubules.
source: While in the fungus Ustilago maydis and Ptk1 cells, spindle elongation is mainly achieved through cortical pulling forces acting on astral microtubules (Aist et al., 1993; Fink et al., 2006; Grill et al., 2001), these forces are not present or dispensable in a plethora of other species.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In yeast, Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, plants, and human, spindle elongation is realized by the generation of microtubule sliding forces at the spindle midzone.
source: In yeast, Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, plants, and human, spindle elongation is realized by the generation of microtubule sliding forces at the spindle midzone (Euteneuer et al., 1982; Khodjakov et al., 2004; Kiyomitsu and Cheeseman, 2013; Redemann et al., 2017; Sharp et al., 1999; Tolić-Nørrelykke et al., 2004; Vukušić et al., 2019; Yu et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The spindle midzone refers to the microtubule overlap at the spindle center, formed by antiparallel-oriented microtubules (interpolar microtubules), which originate from the two opposite spindle poles.
source: The spindle midzone refers to the microtubule overlap at the spindle center, formed by antiparallel-oriented microtubules (interpolar microtubules), which originate from the two opposite spindle poles (Ding et al., 1993; Euteneuer et al., 1982; Mastronarde et al., 1993; McDonald et al., 1977; McIntosh and Landis, 1971; Ward et al., 2014; Winey et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Microtubule sliding is promoted by members of the kinesin-5 family in most organisms.
source: Microtubule sliding is promoted by members of the kinesin-5 family in most organisms (Avunie-Masala et al., 2011; Brust-Mascher et al., 2009; Saunders et al., 1995; Sharp et al., 2000; Straight et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The tetrameric kinesin crosslinks antiparallel microtubules and slides them apart.
source: The tetrameric kinesin crosslinks antiparallel microtubules and slides them apart (Avunie-Masala et al., 2011; Brust-Mascher et al., 2009; Kapitein et al., 2005; Saunders et al., 1995; Shimamoto et al., 2015; Straight et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: By walking toward the microtubule plus-ends of each of the two microtubules that it crosslinks, kinesin-5 can move the microtubules relative to each other.
source: By walking toward the microtubule plus-ends of each of the two microtubules, that it crosslinks, kinesin-5 can move the microtubules relative to each other (Kapitein et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In fission yeast, the kinesin-6 Klp9 mainly performs the task of microtubule sliding, localizing to the spindle midzone upon anaphase B onset.
source: In fission yeast, this task is mainly performed by the kinesin-6 Klp9, which localizes to the spindle midzone upon anaphase B onset (Fu et al., 2009; Krüger et al., 2019; Rincon et al., 2017; Yukawa et al., 2019a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The kinesin-5 Cut7 also generates microtubule sliding forces, but to a lower extent than Klp9.
source: The kinesin-5 Cut7 also generates microtubule sliding forces, but to a lower extent than Klp9 (Rincon et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In the absence of both sliding motors (Klp9 and Cut7), spindle elongation is abolished, leading to 'cut' of chromosomes by the cytokinetic ring and mis-segregated chromosomes.
source: In the absence of both sliding motors, spindle elongation is abolished, leading to 'cut' of chromosomes by the cytokinetic ring and mis-segregated chromosomes (Rincon et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Concomitantly with microtubule sliding, the interpolar microtubules have to grow at a rate that allows the spindle to elongate while maintaining the spindle midzone.
source: Concomitantly with microtubule sliding, the interpolar microtubules have to grow at a rate that allows the spindle to elongate while maintaining the spindle midzone (Cande and McDonald, 1986; Cande and McDonald, 1985; Cheerambathur et al., 2007; Masuda, 1995; Masuda and Cande, 1987; Saxton and McIntosh, 1987).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Microtubule growth has to occur with at least the velocity the spindle microtubules slide apart to keep the microtubule overlap, necessary for spindle stability.
source: Microtubule growth has to occur with at least the velocity the spindle microtubules slide apart to keep the microtubule overlap, necessary for spindle stability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the requirement to maintain spindle midzone during elongation.

claim: Microtubule dynamics during anaphase B have been shown to be regulated by CLASP, which promotes microtubule polymerization or increases the frequency of microtubule rescues.
source: Microtubule dynamics during anaphase B have been shown to be regulated by CLASP, which promotes microtubule polymerization or increases the frequency of microtubule rescues (Bratman and Chang, 2007; Maton et al., 2015; Pereira et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Silencing of the transforming acid coiled-coil (TACC) protein TACC3 reduces the rate of spindle elongation by destabilizing midzone microtubules.
source: Moreover, silencing of the transforming acid coiled-coil (TACC) protein TACC3, which stabilizes microtubules together with XMAP215 (Gergely et al., 2003; Kinoshita et al., 2005; Peset et al., 2005), reduces the rate of spindle elongation by destabilizing midzone microtubules (Lioutas and Vernos, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: TACC3 stabilizes microtubules together with XMAP215.
source: Moreover, silencing of the transforming acid coiled-coil (TACC) protein TACC3, which stabilizes microtubules together with XMAP215 (Gergely et al., 2003; Kinoshita et al., 2005; Peset et al., 2005), reduces the rate of spindle elongation by destabilizing midzone microtubules (Lioutas and Vernos, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Precise regulation of microtubule stability is necessary for proper spindle elongation.
source: This strongly suggests that precise regulation of microtubule stability is necessary for proper spindle elongation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that TACC3 silencing affects spindle elongation.

claim: In animal cells, the kinesin-4 member Kif4a terminates anaphase B spindle elongation by promoting the inhibition of microtubule polymerization and thus restricting spindle midzone length.
source: Accordingly, in animal cells, the kinesin-4 member Kif4a terminates anaphase B spindle elongation by promoting the inhibition of microtubule polymerization and thus restricting spindle midzone length (Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Xenopus kinesin-5 promotes microtubule polymerization in vitro.
source: Supporting this possibility, Xenopus kinesin-5 promotes microtubule polymerization in vitro (Chen and Hancock, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Xenopus kinesin-5 has been proposed to induce a curved-to-straight conformational transition of tubulin at microtubule plus-ends, thus promoting microtubule growth by virtue of a stabilizing effect.
source: The motor has been proposed to induce a curved-to-straight conformational transition of tubulin at microtubule plus-ends, thus promoting microtubule growth by virtue of a stabilizing effect (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Klp9 sets the velocity of spindle elongation in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Moreover, Klp9 sets the velocity of spindle elongation in a dose-dependent manner (Krüger et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Spindles elongate faster as the amount of Klp9 motors increases at the spindle midzone.
source: Spindles elongate faster as the amount of motors increases at the spindle midzone.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work showing dose-dependent effect of Klp9.

claim: Klp9 recruitment to spindle microtubules is regulated in a dephosphorylation-dependent manner by the microtubule polymerase Dis1, homolog of XMAP215 and ch-TOG.
source: Klp9 recruitment to spindle microtubules is regulated in a dephosphorylation-dependent manner by the microtubule polymerase Dis1, homolog of XMAP215 and ch-TOG (Matsuo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing Dis1-dependent Klp9 recruitment and citation to previous work on Dis1.

claim: Monopolar spindles can be generated by the temperature-sensitive mutant cut7-24.
source: Monopolar spindles can be generated by the temperature-sensitive mutant cut7-24 (Hagan and Yanagida, 1992; Hagan and Yanagida, 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The kinesin-5 Cut7 is essential to establish spindle bipolarity during spindle assembly by separating the two spindle poles.
source: Since the kinesin-5 Cut7 is essential to establish spindle bipolarity during spindle assembly by separating the two spindle poles (Hagan and Yanagida, 1992), inactivation of Cut7 at its restrictive temperature results in the formation of monopolar spindles (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Inactivation of Cut7 at its restrictive temperature results in the formation of monopolar spindles.
source: Since the kinesin-5 Cut7 is essential to establish spindle bipolarity during spindle assembly by separating the two spindle poles (Hagan and Yanagida, 1992), inactivation of Cut7 at its restrictive temperature results in the formation of monopolar spindles (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation and data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In cut7-24 cells, microtubule bundles grew up to an average length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm.
source: The bundles grew up to an average length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm, which is slightly longer than half of the average wild-type spindle length (11.6 ± 1.3 µm) (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The average wild-type spindle length is 11.6 ± 1.3 µm.
source: The bundles grew up to an average length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm, which is slightly longer than half of the average wild-type spindle length (11.6 ± 1.3 µm) (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In cut7-24 cells, microtubule bundles grew with an average speed of 0.7 ± 0.2 µm/min.
source: The bundles grew up to an average length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm, which is slightly longer than half of the average wild-type spindle length (11.6 ± 1.3 µm) (Figure 1B) with an average speed of 0.7 ± 0.2 µm/min, slightly faster than half of the velocity at which the bipolar wild-type spindle elongated (1.2 ± 0.2 µm/min) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—source data 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The bipolar wild-type spindle elongated with a velocity of 1.2 ± 0.2 µm/min.
source: The bundles grew up to an average length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm, which is slightly longer than half of the average wild-type spindle length (11.6 ± 1.3 µm) (Figure 1B) with an average speed of 0.7 ± 0.2 µm/min, slightly faster than half of the velocity at which the bipolar wild-type spindle elongated (1.2 ± 0.2 µm/min) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—source data 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Monopolar spindles appear to behave like half-spindles.
source: Thus, monopolar spindles appear to behave like half-spindles.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that monopolar spindle bundle length and velocity are approximately half of bipolar spindle values.

claim: The growth velocity of individual bundles increased with final bundle length in cut7-24 cells.
source: Moreover, the growth velocity of individual bundles increased with final bundle length (Figure 1C, Figure 1—source data 1), a correlation we have previously observed for bipolar anaphase B spindles: longer spindles elongate with respectively higher velocities (Krüger et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Longer spindles elongate with respectively higher velocities.
source: Moreover, the growth velocity of individual bundles increased with final bundle length (Figure 1C, Figure 1—source data 1), a correlation we have previously observed for bipolar anaphase B spindles: longer spindles elongate with respectively higher velocities (Krüger et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cdc13 disappears from spindle microtubules just before anaphase B onset.
source: Cdc13 disappears from spindle microtubules just before anaphase B onset (Decottignies et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Fading of the Cdc13-GFP signal on wild-type spindle microtubules and cut7-24 monopolar spindle microtubules was observed just before the spindle or bundle was elongated.
source: Accordingly, we observed fading of the signal on wild-type spindle microtubules and cut7-24 monopolar spindle microtubules just before the spindle or bundle was elongated (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In bipolar spindles, the sliding motor Klp9 (kinesin-6) localizes to the spindle midzone from anaphase B onset.
source: In bipolar spindles, the sliding motor Klp9 (kinesin-6) localizes to the spindle midzone from anaphase B onset (Fu et al., 2009; Figure 1E, left panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation and data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In the cut7-24 monopolar spindle, Klp9-GFP localized to the tip of the microtubule bundle once it started to elongate.
source: In the cut7-24 monopolar spindle, Klp9-GFP localized to the tip of the microtubule bundle once it started to elongate (Figure 1E, right panel, asterisk).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Klp9-GFP preferentially localized to the tip of the bundle from the first time point of bundle elongation.
source: The Klp9-GFP intensity profile obtained at three different time points of anphase B revealed that Klp9-GFP preferentially localized to the tip of the bundle from the first time point of bundle elongation (Figure 1F)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The Klp9-GFP intensity increased with anaphase B progression in monopolar spindles.
source: The Klp9-GFP intensity profile obtained at three different time points of anphase B revealed that Klp9-GFP preferentially localized to the tip of the bundle from the first time point of bundle elongation (Figure 1F) and the intensity increased with anaphase B progression (Figure 1F,G, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1F and 1G.

claim: While the bundle was growing, Klp9 accumulated at its tip.
source: Hence, while the bundle was growing Klp9 accumulated at its tip.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Klp9-GFP intensity increased at the bundle tip during bundle growth.

claim: A strong correlation of the Klp9-GFP intensity at the bundle tip and the bundle length was observed.
source: In general, we observed a strong correlation of the Klp9-GFP intensity at the bundle tip and the bundle length (Figure 1H, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Ase1 crosslinks the antiparallel-overlapping microtubules at the spindle center and stabilizes the spindle structure.
source: Ase1 crosslinks the antiparallel-overlapping microtubules at the spindle center and stabilizes the spindle structure (Janson et al., 2007; Loïodice et al., 2005; Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the wild-type spindle, Ase1-GFP localized to the spindle midzone just before anaphase B onset and onward.
source: In the wild-type spindle, Ase1-GFP localized to the spindle midzone just before anaphase B onset and onward, as previously reported (Loïodice et al., 2005; Figure 1I, left panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation and data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: In the monopolar spindle, Ase1-GFP localized to the spindle just before the microtubule bundle started to grow.
source: In the monopolar spindle, Ase1-GFP similarly localized to the spindle just before the microtubule bundle started to grow (Figure 1I, right panel, asterisk).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The Ase1-GFP signal was spread all along the bundle at early time points of bundle elongation.
source: The signal was spread all along the bundle at early time points of bundle elongation (Figure 1I,J; timepoint 1), and accumulated at the bundle tip at later time points (Figure 1I,J; timepoint 2 and 3, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1I and 1J.

claim: Ase1-GFP accumulated at the bundle tip at later time points of bundle elongation.
source: The signal was spread all along the bundle at early time points of bundle elongation (Figure 1I,J; timepoint 1), and accumulated at the bundle tip at later time points (Figure 1I,J; timepoint 2 and 3, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1I and 1J.

claim: Klp9 may transport Ase1, as the motor has previously been shown to physically interact with the crosslinker.
source: Klp9 may transport Ase1, as the motor has previously been shown to physically interact with the crosslinker (Fu et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on previous observation of physical interaction between Klp9 and Ase1.

claim: Cut7-24 monopolar spindles proceed to anaphase B, as judged by the absence of the Cdc13-GFP signal, and the presence of Klp9-GFP and Ase1-GFP on growing microtubule bundles.
source: Taken together, besides unseparated spindle poles, cut7-24 monopolar spindles proceed to anaphase B, as judged by the absence of the Cdc13-GFP signal, and the presence of Klp9-GFP and Ase1-GFP on growing microtubule bundles (Figure 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1K and previous figures.

claim: Initiation of anaphase B in cut7-24 mutant, despite unsegregated DNA, appears to be the result of a leaky checkpoint at the metaphase-to-anaphase transition.
source: Initiation of anaphase B, despite unsegregated DNA in this mutant (Hagan and Yanagida, 1990), appears to be the result of a leaky checkpoint at the metaphase-to-anaphase transition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that anaphase B occurs despite unsegregated DNA.

claim: After 1–2 hr, cut7-24 cells will proceed to anaphase B irrespectively of unseparated spindle poles or DNA.
source: After 1–2 hr, cut7-24 cells will proceed to anaphase B irrespectively of unseparated spindle poles or DNA.
evidence: The claim is based on observations of cut7-24 cell behavior.

claim: During anaphase B in cut7-24 cells, long microtubule bundles are polymerized with a bundle growth velocity that equals half of the spindle elongation velocity of bipolar spindles.
source: During this phase long microtubule bundles are polymerized with a bundle growth velocity that equals half of the spindle elongation velocity of bipolar spindles, suggesting that microtubule dynamics are not altered in the mutant and regulated independently of microtubule sliding forces.
evidence: The claim is supported by data comparing bundle growth velocity in monopolar spindles to spindle elongation velocity in bipolar spindles.

claim: Microtubule dynamics are not altered in the cut7-24 mutant and regulated independently of microtubule sliding forces.
source: During this phase long microtubule bundles are polymerized with a bundle growth velocity that equals half of the spindle elongation velocity of bipolar spindles, suggesting that microtubule dynamics are not altered in the mutant and regulated independently of microtubule sliding forces.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that bundle growth velocity matches expected values.

claim: Monopolar spindles constitute a suitable tool to study microtubule dynamics during anaphase B.
source: Therefore, monopolar spindles constitute a suitable tool to study microtubule dynamics during anaphase B.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the characterization of monopolar spindles showing they proceed to anaphase B with expected microtubule dynamics.

claim: Deletion of klp9 strongly decreased the speed of bipolar spindle elongation in anaphase B.
source: As reported earlier (Fu et al., 2009), deletion of klp9 strongly decreased the speed of bipolar spindle elongation in anaphase B (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation and data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Deletion of klp9 in the cut7-24 background prevented the formation of long microtubule bundles.
source: Deletion of klp9 in the cut7-24 background prevented the formation of long microtubule bundles (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: While anaphase B microtubule bundles reached a maximum length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm in the presence of Klp9, the bundles only grew up to 2.7 ± 0.5 µm upon klp9 deletion.
source: While anaphase B microtubule bundles reached a maximum length of 6.1 ± 1.0 µm in the presence of Klp9, the bundles only grew up to 2.7 ± 0.5 µm upon klp9 deletion (Figure 2C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The growth velocity of the bundles was strongly reduced in klp9 deleted cells (cut7-24: 0.7 ± 0.2 µm/min; cut7-24 klp9Δ: 0.1 ± 0.1 µm/min).
source: Moreover, the growth velocity of the bundles was strongly reduced in klp9 deleted cells (cut7-24: 0.7 ± 0.2 µm/min; cut7-24 klp9Δ: 0.1 ± 0.1 µm/min) (Figure 2C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In the klp9 shut-off strain, the bundles reached a maximum length of 3.2 ± 0.8 µm and grew with an average velocity of 0.2 ± 0.2 µm/min.
source: Indeed, the phenotype was slightly less dramatic as compared to the deletion of klp9 (Figure 1C). The bundles reached a maximum length of 3.2 ± 0.8 µm and grew with an average velocity of 0.2 ± 0.2 µm/min.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the klp9 shut-off strain.

claim: Klp9 is involved in the regulation of microtubule growth during anaphase B.
source: Together, this suggests that Klp9 is involved in the regulation of microtubule growth during anaphase B.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that klp9 deletion reduces microtubule bundle growth.

claim: Klp9 has been previously implicated in the regulation of the metaphase-to-anaphase B transition.
source: However, Klp9 has been previously implicated in the regulation of the metaphase-to-anaphase B transition (Meadows et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In a bipolar klp9Δ spindle, Cdc13-GFP disappeared from the spindle just before initiation of anaphase B spindle elongation.
source: In a bipolar klp9Δ spindle, Cdc13-GFP disappeared from the spindle just before initiation of anaphase B spindle elongation (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the cut7-24 klp9Δ mutant, Cdc13-GFP disappeared from the spindle microtubules, but still no long microtubule bundle was formed.
source: In the cut7-24 klp9Δ mutant, Cdc13-GFP also disappeared from the spindle microtubules, but still no long microtubule bundle was formed (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The observed phenotype upon klp9 deletion can be attributed to the Klp9 function in microtubule growth regulation during anaphase B.
source: Hence, the observed phenotype can be attributed to the Klp9 function in microtubule growth regulation during anaphase B.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that anaphase B transition occurs normally in klp9Δ cells but microtubule growth is impaired.

claim: Deletion of dis1 led to a decrease of the bundle growth velocity comparable to the deletion or shut-off condition of klp9.
source: However, only the deletion of dis1 led to a decrease of the bundle growth velocity comparable to the deletion or shut-off condition of klp9 (Figure 3B,C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Maximum bundle length was reduced upon deletion of ase1, dis1, and alp7, with the strongest decrease observed upon dis1 deletion.
source: Moreover, maximum bundle length was reduced upon deletion of ase1, dis1, and alp7, with the strongest decrease observed upon dis1 deletion (Figure 3D, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Of the tested candidates, the deletion of dis1 gave rise to a similar phenotype as the deletion or shut-off condition of klp9.
source: Taken together, of the tested candidates, the deletion of dis1 gave rise to a similar phenotype as the deletion or shut-off condition of klp9.
evidence: The claim is supported by data comparing effects of various deletions on microtubule bundle growth.

claim: Like Klp9, Dis1 seems to be involved in the regulation of microtubule growth during anaphase B and may act in the same pathway with Klp9.
source: Thus, like Klp9, Dis1 seems to be involved in the regulation of microtubule growth during anaphase B and may act in the same pathway with Klp9.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the similar phenotypes observed upon deletion of klp9 and dis1.

claim: Cut7 has been shown to promote spindle elongation like Klp9, even though to a lower extent.
source: Cut7 has been shown to promote spindle elongation like Klp9, even though to a lower extent (Rincon et al., 2017; Yukawa et al., 2019b)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A dimeric construct of the X. laevis kinesin-5 Eg5 promotes microtubule growth in vitro.
source: Cut7 has been shown to promote spindle elongation like Klp9, even though to a lower extent (Rincon et al., 2017; Yukawa et al., 2019b), and a dimeric construct of the X. laevis kinesin-5 Eg5 promotes microtubule growth in vitro (Chen et al., 2019; Chen and Hancock, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Sad1-1 monopolar spindles assembled long microtubule bundles during anaphase B.
source: Sad1-1 monopolar spindles also assembled long microtubule bundles during anaphase B (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Sad1-1 monopolar spindles can be used to study microtubule dynamics during anaphase B.
source: Thus, sad1-1 monopolar spindles can also be used to study microtubule dynamics during anaphase B.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that sad1-1 monopolar spindles behave similarly to cut7-24 monopolar spindles.

claim: Deletion of cut7 (cut7Δpkl1Δ) led to a slight increase of the growth velocity.
source: Unlike the deletion of klp9 or dis1, the deletion of cut7 (cut7Δpkl1Δ) led to a slight increase of the growth velocity (Figure 3F, H)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3F and 3H.

claim: The modest acceleration of bundle growth upon cut7 deletion seemed to be a result of the absence of Cut7 and not Pkl1.
source: The modest acceleration of bundle growth seemed to be a result of the absence of Cut7 and not Pkl1, since the deletion of pkl1 alone did not affect growth velocity significantly (Figure 3F, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3F comparing cut7Δpkl1Δ and pkl1Δ.

claim: While Klp9-GFP was detected at the tip of microtubule bundles, Cut7-GFP localized only to the unseparated spindle poles in sad1-1 mutant.
source: Furthermore, we investigated the localization of Cut7-GFP in the sad1-1 mutant. While, Klp9-GFP was detected at the tip of microtubule bundles, Cut7-GFP localized only to the unseparated spindle poles (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Only Klp9 tracks the tip of the microtubule bundles in monopolar spindles, and promotes their growth during anaphase B.
source: Thus, even though both motors have been reported to be plus-end directed bipolar kinesins, and both localize to spindle microtubules in a bipolar spindle (Fu et al., 2009; Hagan and Yanagida, 1992), only Klp9 tracks the tip of the microtubule bundles in monopolar spindles, and promotes their growth during anaphase B.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential localization of Klp9 and Cut7 in monopolar spindles.

claim: Cut7, like other kinesin-5 members, has been shown to move bidirectionally along microtubule tracks.
source: Cut7, like other kinesin-5 members, has been shown to move bidirectionally along microtubule tracks (Edamatsu, 2014; Roostalu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Bidirectional motility may be the basis for the differential localization of Cut7.
source: This bidirectional motility may be the basis for the differential localization of Cut7.
